literature_proposed.summary: No proof is known. The statement says that for infinitely many N the fractional part of F_N = sum_{n=2}^N N!/(n!-1) is at most 1 - 1/N. Its position on the record: it is implied by erdos-68--h3 (which asks for < 1 - 2/N), and with the proved tail bound erdos-68--h5 (1/(N+1) < N!S - F_N < 1/N for N >= 4) it implies erdos-68--h6 and so the irrationality of S. Neither reverse implication is known. Two checks bound it. (1) It does not follow from h3's shape alone: with S's own tail, a real whose factorial digits are 0 except a digit n-1 at every fourth place fails h3's inequality at every N >= 4 but meets this one infinitely often. (2) It is stronger than the root as far as anyone knows: if T = S - (e - 2) = sum_{n>=2} 1/(n!(n!-1)) were rational, S would still be irrational, yet F_N's fractional part would be 1 - O(1/((N+1)(N+1)!)) for all large N, so this statement would fail. Any proof of it therefore also proves that T is irrational, which is not known either.
